chapter_note: A two-part chapter. The first half (i=0-36) is a polemical narrative: Mani the Illuminator encounters an old presbyter of "the doctrine of Sin" (an idol-serving sect — likely Magousaean/Babylonian temple cult) and uses a fruit-on-tree parable to argue that the presbyter is rightly called 'son of sin' as long as he remains in the cosmos. This entire encounter is editorial — anti-heretical polemic plus hortatory application woven into a Mani-vs-priest dialogue. The second half (i=42-77, badly damaged at 87% damage ratio) shifts dramatically into cosmological substrate enumeration: Great Mind, Youth, twelve angels, twenty-two angels, seven pillars, four angels supporting the cosmos, five gods/food of man, the Calling and Hearing, Adamas of Light, twelve powers/likenesses, three great pillars of strength, firmaments, Omophoros. The editorial fatigue score (-6.31) confirms the structural pattern: editorial vocabulary front-loaded in the first half, substrate vocabulary emerging in the second half — atypical because it's the substrate teaching that has been APPENDED to a polemical narrative frame, rather than the usual reverse. The "holy Church" of i=35 and i=57 marks ecclesial intrusions.
